metadata.source: Invest Aaj For Kal - Anant Ladha Option Course
metadata.purpose: F&O LLM system prompt knowledge base

core_philosophy.primary_goal: Generate regular monthly income from options, not speculative one-time gains
core_philosophy.seller_advantage: Option sellers win ~70-80% of the time due to time decay (theta). The house always wins.
core_philosophy.key_principle: Sell options when IV is high, buy when IV is low. Never reverse this.
core_philosophy.risk_mindset: Define maximum loss BEFORE entering any trade. Never let a loss run without a stop.
core_philosophy.capital_rule: Never deploy more than 20-25% of capital in a single options position
core_philosophy.consistency_over_bigwin: A consistent 3-5% monthly return beats chasing 50% in one trade

option_basics.CE: Call European - right to BUY underlying at strike price
option_basics.PE: Put European - right to SELL underlying at strike price
option_basics.option_buyer: Pays premium, has unlimited upside, limited loss (premium paid). Wins only on big directional moves.
option_basics.option_seller: Receives premium, has limited profit (premium received), theoretically unlimited loss. Wins when market stays stable.

moneyness.ITM: In The Money - strike has intrinsic value, expensive, high delta
moneyness.ATM: At The Money - strike nearest to current price, highest time value
moneyness.OTM: Out of The Money - no intrinsic value, cheap, low delta, preferred for selling

delta.definition: How much option price moves for every 1 point move in underlying
delta.range: 0 to 1 for calls, 0 to -1 for puts
delta.trading_use: Sell options with delta 0.15-0.25 for high probability of profit (~75-85%)
delta.delta_neutral: When total delta of position = 0. Market direction doesn't matter. Pure theta play.

theta.definition: Time decay - how much option premium erodes every day
theta.seller_benefit: Theta works FOR option sellers. Every day that passes, seller profits.
theta.acceleration: Theta decay accelerates in last 7 days before expiry - maximum decay near expiry
theta.ATM_theta: Highest at ATM strikes - avoid buying ATM unless expecting big move
theta.strategy: Sell options with high theta. Weekly expiry = faster theta decay = faster income
theta.anant_rule: The last 2-3 days before expiry, 70% of remaining premium decays. Sellers' golden window.

vega.seller_impact: When IV drops, option premiums drop - PROFITS for seller even without price move
vega.buyer_impact: IV crush after events (budget, RBI policy, results) destroys option buyer premiums
vega.rule: Sell options when IV is HIGH (before events). Buy when IV is LOW.

gamma.definition: Rate of change of delta. How fast delta accelerates.
gamma.seller_risk: High gamma = dangerous for sellers near expiry. Big moves can wipe out profit fast.
gamma.rule: Square off selling positions by Wednesday/Thursday if expiry is near and market is volatile

structure.ATM_identification: Strike closest to current spot price. Usually highlighted.

open_interest.definition: Total outstanding contracts at a strike. Higher OI = more significant level.
open_interest.call_OI_wall: Strike with HIGHEST Call OI = strong RESISTANCE. Market unlikely to cross above it.
open_interest.put_OI_wall: Strike with HIGHEST Put OI = strong SUPPORT. Market unlikely to fall below it.
open_interest.fresh_buildup: OI increasing + price rising = fresh longs (bullish signal)
open_interest.short_covering: OI decreasing + price rising = shorts covering (weak/temporary bounce)
open_interest.long_unwinding: OI decreasing + price falling = longs exiting (bearish signal)
open_interest.anant_rule: The strikes with max OI define your trading range for the week/month

change_in_OI.definition: How OI changed from previous session
change_in_OI.positive_change_calls: New call writing = sellers expect market to stay below this strike (bearish above)
change_in_OI.positive_change_puts: New put writing = sellers expect market to stay above this strike (bullish below)
change_in_OI.reading: Track CHANGE in OI, not just absolute OI. Fresh positions matter more.

put_call_ratio.formula: PCR = Total Put OI / Total Call OI
put_call_ratio.bullish: PCR > 1.2 → More puts written → writers confident market will hold → BULLISH
put_call_ratio.bearish: PCR < 0.8 → More calls written → writers expect market to stay down → BEARISH
put_call_ratio.neutral: PCR 0.9 to 1.1 → Sideways market expected → good for Iron Condor / Strangle
put_call_ratio.contrarian_use: Extreme PCR > 1.5 = overly bullish = potential reversal warning
put_call_ratio.anant_rule: PCR between 1.0-1.3 is the sweet spot for selling both sides (non-directional)

implied_volatility.definition: Market's expectation of future volatility priced into options
implied_volatility.high_iv: IV > 20% = Premiums are fat. SELL options. This is the seller's market.
implied_volatility.low_iv: IV < 13% = Premiums are thin. Poor time to sell. Consider buying.
implied_volatility.iv_skew: Put IV usually higher than Call IV (market fears downside more) - NORMAL
implied_volatility.reverse_skew: Call IV > Put IV = Market expects upside breakout - unusual, be cautious
implied_volatility.anant_rule: Always check India VIX before selling. VIX below 14 = low premium, not worth selling naked

india_vix.definition: India's fear index. Measures expected volatility of Nifty over next 30 days.
india_vix.low_vix: VIX < 13 → Market calm → Low premiums → Prefer buying or avoid selling
india_vix.medium_vix: VIX 13-18 → Normal → Good for most selling strategies
india_vix.high_vix: VIX 18-25 → Elevated fear → Fat premiums → BEST for selling, but add protection
india_vix.extreme_vix: VIX > 25 → Panic → Premiums very fat BUT market can move violently. Sell spreads not naked.

max_pain.definition: Strike at which maximum number of option buyers lose money at expiry
max_pain.market_tendency: Market gravitates toward max pain as expiry approaches (option writers are institutions)
max_pain.use: If max pain is 19400 and market is at 19600, lean bearish going into expiry
max_pain.anant_rule: Max pain is not a guarantee but a probability magnet. Use as bias, not as target.

reading_process.step1: Check India VIX first - determines whether to buy or sell
reading_process.step2: Identify ATM strike - your reference point
reading_process.step3: Find highest Call OI strike = resistance
reading_process.step4: Find highest Put OI strike = support
reading_process.step6: Check OI changes - where fresh money is going
reading_process.step8: Identify your trading range for the week
reading_process.step9: Select strikes OUTSIDE this range for selling
reading_process.step10: Check max pain for expiry day bias

covered_call.description: Own underlying stock + sell OTM call against it. Classic income strategy.
covered_call.best_market: Neutral to mildly bullish. Works poorly in strongly trending markets.
covered_call.income_potential: 1-3% monthly on stock value in normal volatility environments

entry_rules.own_the_stock: MUST own at least 1 lot equivalent of the stock (not index)
entry_rules.stock_selection: Only on liquid F&O stocks you're happy holding long-term: RELIANCE, INFY, TCS, HDFC Bank, ITC, WIPRO
entry_rules.timing: Sell on Monday morning after checking option chain. Capture full week theta.
entry_rules.iv_condition: Only sell when IV is above stock's 30-day historical volatility
entry_rules.expiry: Monthly expiry preferred for covered calls (more premium, less monitoring)

exit_rules.profit_target: Buy back call when 50-70% of premium is captured (don't be greedy for last 30%)
exit_rules.loss_rule: If stock rises and call goes deep ITM, buy back call and roll up to higher strike
exit_rules.rolling_up: If stock rises beyond strike: buy back current call, sell higher strike call for next expiry
exit_rules.early_exit: If only 2-3 days to expiry and 80%+ premium captured, close and redeploy
exit_rules.stock_called_away: If assigned, sell cash-secured put at lower strike to re-enter position (wheel strategy)

risk_management.max_loss: Unlimited downside on stock position (offset slightly by premium received)
risk_management.opportunity_risk: If stock rockets, you cap gains at strike price + premium
risk_management.mitigation: Only run on blue chip stocks you'd hold anyway. Premium is bonus income.
risk_management.position_size: Never more than 25% of portfolio in covered calls on single stock

wheel_strategy.description: Systematic covered call + cash secured put cycle for continuous income
wheel_strategy.step1: Sell Cash Secured Put at support level (collect premium, potentially buy stock cheap)
wheel_strategy.step2: If assigned stock, immediately sell Covered Call at resistance (collect more premium)
wheel_strategy.step3: If call assigned, stock sold at profit. Restart with cash secured put.
wheel_strategy.income: 2-4% monthly with disciplined execution on quality stocks

short_strangle.description: Sell OTM Call + Sell OTM Put simultaneously. Pure non-directional income.
short_strangle.structure: Short OTM Call + Short OTM Put (same expiry)
short_strangle.best_market: Non-trending, sideways market. PCR near 1.0. VIX 14-20.
short_strangle.profit_condition: Market stays between both strikes at expiry. Both options expire worthless.

entry_rules.instrument: Nifty or BankNifty weekly options (most liquid, tightest spreads)
entry_rules.call_strike: Sell at or just above highest Call OI resistance
entry_rules.put_strike: Sell at or just below highest Put OI support
entry_rules.premium_target: Collect minimum 0.5% of index value total premium. Below this not worth the risk.
entry_rules.vix_condition: VIX between 14-22. Below 14 = too little premium. Above 22 = too risky naked.
entry_rules.timing: Enter Monday morning. Exit by Wednesday afternoon (avoid gamma risk near expiry)

exit_rules.profit_target: Close at 40-50% of max profit (premium collected). Don't hold to full expiry.
exit_rules.stop_loss_call: If call side premium doubles (2x), close entire position
exit_rules.stop_loss_put: If put side premium doubles (2x), close entire position
exit_rules.time_stop: Mandatory close by Wednesday 2:30 PM regardless of P&L (avoid Thursday gamma risk)
exit_rules.adjustment: If one side is threatened, roll it out to next strike or next expiry

risk_management.naked_risk: Unlimited loss if market moves violently beyond your strikes
risk_management.solution: Convert to Iron Condor by buying further OTM options as protection (recommended)
risk_management.margin: Requires significant margin - check SPAN margin on Sensibull before entry
risk_management.max_positions: Max 2 strangle positions simultaneously. Concentration kills.

iron_condor.description: Short Strangle + protection wings. Defined risk, regular income. Anant's preferred strategy.
iron_condor.structure: Sell OTM Call + Buy further OTM Call + Sell OTM Put + Buy further OTM Put
iron_condor.best_market: Sideways to mildly trending. Best in medium VIX (14-20).
iron_condor.advantage_over_strangle: Defined maximum loss. Lower margin requirement. Sleep well at night.

entry_rules.instrument: Nifty monthly options (more stable than weekly for condor)
entry_rules.sell_call: Sell at resistance (highest Call OI strike). Delta ~0.20
entry_rules.buy_call: Buy 200-300 points above sell call (protection wing)
entry_rules.sell_put: Sell at support (highest Put OI strike). Delta ~0.20
entry_rules.buy_put: Buy 200-300 points below sell put (protection wing)
entry_rules.net_premium: Minimum ₹80-100 per lot after buying protection wings
entry_rules.wing_width: Wider wings = more protection but less premium. 200 points standard for Nifty.
entry_rules.risk_reward: Target 1:1.5 risk:reward minimum. Risk ₹100 to make ₹150 net premium.

exit_rules.profit_target: Close at 50% of max profit. Don't be greedy.
exit_rules.adjustment_call_side: If Nifty approaches sell call strike: roll call spread up by 200-300 points
exit_rules.adjustment_put_side: If Nifty approaches sell put strike: roll put spread down by 200-300 points
exit_rules.max_loss_rule: If position hits 2x premium received in loss, close entire position
exit_rules.time_based_exit: Close entire position 5 days before expiry (avoid gamma risk)

zero_risk_strategy.description: PR Sundar's strategy - sell ATM option and buy 2x OTM options. Net zero or small credit.
zero_risk_strategy.structure: Sell 1 ATM CE + Buy 2 OTM CEs (or same for puts)
zero_risk_strategy.logic: Premium from selling 1 ATM finances buying 2 OTM. If market moves big, OTM gains > ATM loss.
zero_risk_strategy.best_market: High volatility events - Budget, Results, RBI policy
zero_risk_strategy.anant_note: Called '0 risk' because max loss is zero or small debit. But opportunity cost is real.
zero_risk_strategy.entry: Enter before event when IV is elevated. ATM premium is fat.
zero_risk_strategy.exit: Exit after event announcement when IV collapses (within 30-60 minutes of event)
zero_risk_strategy.key_risk: IV crush post-event can make OTM worthless even if market moves moderately

dhrishyam_strategy.description: Non-directional strategy for sideways markets. Named after the movie (no direction).
dhrishyam_strategy.structure: Short Straddle (sell ATM CE + sell ATM PE) with dynamic adjustment
dhrishyam_strategy.best_market: Absolutely range-bound market. Low VIX. No major events.
dhrishyam_strategy.premium_collection: ATM options have maximum time value. Collect maximum premium.
dhrishyam_strategy.adjustment_rule: If market moves beyond 1 SD, convert one side to spread to limit loss
dhrishyam_strategy.anant_rule: Dhrishyam only when VIX < 14 and no event in next 7 days. Otherwise avoid.
dhrishyam_strategy.risk: Highest risk of all selling strategies. Market gaps can cause severe loss.

bumper_returns_strategy.description: Directional option selling combined with option chain confirmation
bumper_returns_strategy.setup: Strong directional bias confirmed by option chain + TA breakout
bumper_returns_strategy.entry: Sell OTM options on the OPPOSITE side of direction (sell puts in uptrend, sell calls in downtrend)
confirmation_required: OI addition on the direction side
bumper_returns_strategy.strike: Sell 1 SD away from current price in the direction of resistance
bumper_returns_strategy.target: 3-5x premium in 2-3 days on directional moves

when_to_buy.iv_condition: Buy ONLY when IV is low (below 30-day historical volatility)
when_to_buy.vix_condition: VIX below 14 = good time to buy options
when_to_buy.event_based: Buy before event when IV is low, sell after when IV explodes
when_to_buy.trend_based: Strong trending market where 1 SD moves are common

kunal_saraogi_strategy.name: Regular income with option buying
kunal_saraogi_strategy.approach: Buy options at strong support/resistance. Tight stop loss. Multiple small wins.
kunal_saraogi_strategy.key_rule: Never spend more than 1-2% of capital on single option buy
kunal_saraogi_strategy.target: 3:1 reward:risk minimum on every option buy
kunal_saraogi_strategy.instrument: Only buy Nifty/BankNifty options, not stocks (more liquid)

brahmastra_2_strategy.setup: Wait for 9:15-9:30 AM opening range. Enter breakout of opening range high/low.
brahmastra_2_strategy.instrument: BankNifty weekly options (most volatile, best for intraday)
brahmastra_2_strategy.strike: Buy ATM or 1 strike OTM in the direction of breakout
brahmastra_2_strategy.time_stop: Exit by 1:30 PM if target not hit

scalping_strategy.description: Quick 5-15 minute option trades with ₹10,000 capital
scalping_strategy.instrument: BankNifty or Nifty weekly (0DTE or 1DTE near expiry)
scalping_strategy.entry: Enter on 5-minute chart breakout with volume confirmation
scalping_strategy.capital_rule: Never deploy more than 30% of scalping capital in one trade
scalping_strategy.anant_warning: Scalping is highest risk. Suitable only for experienced traders. Theta kills on 0DTE.

golden_rules: Never sell naked options without a stop loss or protection wing
Never average a losing option selling position - it WILL kill your account
Close losing positions at 2x premium received - no exceptions
Never deploy more than 30% capital in options at any time
Keep 30% cash for adjustments and recovery
Track each trade in a journal - without data you cannot improve
Never trade options on Budget/RBI day without hedges in place
One bad trade can wipe 3 months of income - protect capital first

position_sizing.per_trade_max: 2-3% of total trading capital at risk per trade
position_sizing.single_strategy_max: Not more than 2 Iron Condors or 2 Strangles simultaneously
position_sizing.monthly_income_target: Realistic target: 2-4% monthly on capital deployed in options

common_mistakes_anant: Holding losing positions hoping for recovery - options decay, never hope
Selling options in trending markets without direction bias
Ignoring India VIX before entering selling trades
Not booking profit at 50% - greed kills consistency
Trading without checking option chain first
Using full capital in first week of month, nothing left for adjustments
Confusing option buying with selling psychology - they are completely different games
Trading BankNifty without understanding its volatility vs Nifty

adjustment_techniques.rolling: Move strike to next expiry or further OTM strike when position is threatened
adjustment_techniques.converting_to_spread: When naked position threatened, buy protection to convert to spread
adjustment_techniques.delta_hedging: Buy/sell futures to neutralise directional risk when large move happens
adjustment_techniques.stop_and_reverse: Rare but valid: close losing position and take opposite position if bias changes

trending_market.prefer: Directional spreads (Bull Call Spread or Bear Put Spread), Covered calls on the trend side
trending_market.pcr_signal: PCR moving sharply in one direction

sideways_market.prefer: Iron Condor, Short Strangle, Covered Call
sideways_market.oi_signal: High OI walls on both sides with no breakout attempts

high_volatility_market.prefer: Defined risk spreads, PR Sundar zero-risk structure, or simply stay out
high_volatility_market.opportunity: Fat premiums available but need strict discipline

llm_system_prompt.usage: Copy the section below as system prompt for your F&O LLM chatbot
llm_system_prompt.prompt: You are an expert F&O trading assistant trained on Anant Ladha's (Invest Aaj For Kal) option trading methodology for Indian markets (NSE/BSE). You have deep knowledge of: (1) Option chain analysis - reading OI, change in OI, PCR, IV, max pain and India VIX to determine market range and sentiment; (2) Option selling strategies - Covered Call, Short Strangle, Iron Condor, Dhrishyam Strategy, Zero Risk structure; (3) Option buying strategies - Brahmastra, Kunal Saraogi regular income method, scalping with small capital; (4) Greeks - Delta (target 0.15-0.25 for selling), Theta (seller's friend), Vega (sell high IV, avoid low IV), Gamma (manage near expiry); (5) Risk management - 2x stop loss on premium, 50% profit booking, never average losers, max 30% capital in options. When answering: Always check VIX condition first. Always reference option chain signals. Give specific strikes/deltas where relevant. Flag high-risk conditions. Provide India-specific context (Nifty lot=50, BankNifty lot=15). Default to capital preservation over aggressive returns.

before_every_trade: What is India VIX today? (< 14 = buy, 14-20 = sell, > 20 = spreads only)
What is PCR? (< 0.8 bearish, 0.8-1.2 neutral, > 1.2 bullish)
Is my sell strike OUTSIDE the OI support-resistance range?
What is my maximum loss if wrong?
Have I set my stop loss order?
Is there any major event this week? (Budget/RBI/Results)
Is today within 2 days of expiry? (if yes, extreme caution for selling)
What % of my capital is already deployed in options?
